extracted.intended_audience: non-business public commenters, public-interest advocates, and rulemaking participants seeking to influence administrative rulemaking
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for writing effective substantive comments on proposed regulations so non-business interests can counter business influence by matching specificity, providing empirical/cost estimates, coordinating submissions, and documenting distributional impacts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Match business commenters in specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Generic objections from non-business interests do not move the rule. Effective non-business comments propose specific textual changes at the same level of detail business commenters do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide precise, concrete suggested language or edits the agency could adopt rather than high-level complaints. Anti-patterns include vague pleas or broad statements of principle without actionable text. Scoring guidance: higher marks for verbatim or closely-drafted regulatory text and line-specific edits; lower marks for general exhortations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide quantitative cost or benefit estimates
rubrics_metrics.description: A high-impact non-business comment includes its own quantitative estimate of costs/benefits to challenge industry submissions, rather than asserting harm without numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include numeric estimates, cost-benefit calculations, ranges, or modeling that directly rebut industry-provided figures. Cite data sources, describe methods briefly, and note key assumptions. Anti-patterns: assertions of harm with no numbers or unverifiable claims. Scoring guidance: credit for transparent methodology, credible sources, and sensitivity analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propose specific regulatory text the agency could adopt
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective comments propose specific regulatory text the agency could adopt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Draft statute- or regulation-style wording, provide redline/strike-throughs where feasible, and explain how the suggested language addresses the concern. Examples and rationale increase persuasiveness. Scoring: prioritize clarity, legal/technical plausibility, and ease of adoption by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Make distributional consequences explicit
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-business comments win when they make visible distributional consequences (who pays, who benefits) that business comments have an incentive to omit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify which groups (by income, region, industry, demographic) will bear costs or receive benefits; quantify impacts where possible. Use tables or illustrative scenarios if helpful. Anti-patterns: treating impacts as uniform or failing to identify winners/losers. Scoring: higher for concrete, evidence-backed distributional analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coordinate submissions to establish a credible counterweight
rubrics_metrics.description: Because proportions matter, non-business interests should coordinate to ensure substantive non-business presence in the docket — not necessarily through mass form letters but through multiple, distinct, substantive comments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate across organizations to file multiple distinct, substantive comments that cover different angles or replicate key analyses; cite or align with other non-business submissions to show a coherent opposition. Avoid relying solely on identical form letters. Scoring: reward documented cross-citation, complementary analyses, and demonstrable breadth of substantive filings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify gaps or assumptions in industry submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the comment identify gaps or assumptions in industry submissions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scrutinize industry claims for unsupported assumptions, omitted variables, selective evidence, or methodological flaws and explicitly point them out. Where possible, offer corrective data or alternative assumptions. Anti-patterns: merely asserting that industry is biased without indicating specific flaws. Scoring: credit for precise critique tied to evidence or methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equip the comment with counter-expertise (substantive evidence and credibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rubrics for non-business comments must equip ordinary commenters with counter-expertise, not just civic enthusiasm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include expert co-signers, empirical analyses, citations to peer-reviewed literature, appendices with data/methods, and credible sources that establish technical competence. Where internal expertise is lacking, partner with academics, think tanks, or practitioners. Scoring: higher for demonstrated technical competence, transparent methods, and credible authorship.
